question: Two engines of trains 75 km apart start towards each other at speeds of 13 km/hr and 17 km/hr, respectively. After how much time will they meet each other? (Assume the length of engine is negligible.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the engines are moving towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 13 + 17 = 30 km/hr.

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 75 ÷ 30 = 2.5 hours.

Convert hours to minutes: 2.5 × 60 = 150 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 150 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first engine (S₁) = 13 km/hr

Speed of second engine (S₂) = 17 km/hr

Total distance (D) = 75 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 13 + 17

⇒ Relative Speed = 30 km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 75 ÷ 30

⇒ Time = 2.5 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 2.5 × 60

⇒ Time = 150 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 150 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The total distance is covered collectively by both.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). The faster body catches up with the slower one at this speed.

Speed Conversions

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. Similarly, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.
